title: Slide 1 · Facts and predicates
question: Ava writes, “Could I borrow C1 tomorrow?” Which words tell the clerk what she wants, and what would the clerk still need to check before promising it?
answer: “Borrow C1 tomorrow” identifies the item and day she wants. The clerk still needs evidence that C1 can be lent on that day.

title: Slide 2 · What can the desk tell Ava?
question: If the membership test prints True, what has the desk established?
answer: It has found an entry for Ava’s request for C1. To say she has received the camera, we would also need evidence of a handoff.

title: Slide 3 · Give each claim a name
question: The note says “C1 was requested by Ava.” Which position should C1 occupy in Requested?
answer: C1 is the second argument, the item. The wording of the note changed, but Ava still fills the person position.

title: Slide 4 · Ask a question with a blank
question: How would you answer “Who requested C1?” with these same records?
answer: Fix the item as C1 and read the person from each match. Only the first row has that item, so the answer in this record is Ava.

title: Slide 5 · Leave room for an unknown
question: A note says that Bo requested M1. What does that change about M1’s availability?
answer: It adds a request. Availability is a separate claim, so M1’s availability remains unknown until there is evidence about that claim.

title: Slide 6 · Find the items in Ava’s requests
question: Replace this line: if person == "Ava": with: if person == "Bo": What will print?
answer:
T2
Only the second row names Bo. The loop prints the item from that row.

title: Slide 8 · From this module to the next
question: Lin and Bo each have a separate record of completing camera orientation. A clerk wants the same eligibility policy to cover a new borrower next week. What part of the policy should change from person to person?
answer: Only the borrower’s name should vary. The desk can state one policy for anyone who completes orientation, then apply it when an individual’s orientation record arrives.

title: Office hours · Why give a statement an awkward name like Requested(Ava, C1)?
question: Why give a statement an awkward name like Requested(Ava, C1)?
answer: Imagine that Ava writes “Could I borrow C1?” and Bo writes “I’d like to check out C1.” Once a reader confirms that both students are requesting the camera, the desk can use the same relationship to record both requests. The desk can then ask one precise question about the requester and item. The names alone do not decide whether a new note actually expresses a request.

title: Office hours · Does False in a Python membership test settle whether something happened?
question: Does False in a Python membership test settle whether something happened?
answer: It settles whether that exact entry occurs in the collection you checked. If the log is incomplete, an event can have happened without an entry. Say “I found no matching entry” until you know the log covers every event relevant to your question.

title: Exercise 1
question: Translate “Bo requests tripod T2” into a predicate and explain the two positions.
answer: Requested(Bo, T2). Bo is the requester in the first position and T2 is the item in the second.

title: Exercise 2
question: A record contains Requested(Ava, C1), Requested(Ava, C2), and Requested(Bo, C2). Which question returns Ava and Bo as its answers?
answer: Ask Requested(person, C2). The second and third facts match C2. Reading their person positions gives Ava and Bo.

title: Exercise 3
question: A clerk finds no record of Returned(Ava, C1) and concludes that Ava still has C1. Give two different histories consistent with the missing record.
answer: Ava might still have C1, or she might have returned it before the clerk entered the return. A missing return record alone cannot distinguish those histories.

title: Lab case 1 · One request
question: Which item did Ava request? What evidence would establish a completed loan?
answer: Ava requested C1. Availability says the item is available in the record. A recorded handoff to Ava would establish the completed transfer.

title: Lab case 2 · Second borrower
question: What does the query Requested(person, C1) return now?
answer: It returns both Ava and Bo. Each name fills the blank in a different matching fact. Neither request alone gives an order for allocating C1.

title: Lab case 3 · Explicit status
question: What can the desk tell Ava about C1 and C2?
answer: The desk has a recorded reason to report C1 unavailable. C2’s status is unknown. It would need a status record for C2 before offering it as an available alternative.
